blocks.html: Lesson 5 of 7. "SharePoint" shows up in two ways at OneAccord. Behind your Teams channel files, it's the collaborative space you worked in during Lesson 4. The other is the dedicated SharePoint site called the OneAccord Hub, and that's what this lesson is about.

The OneAccord Hub: your read-only reference library

The Hub holds information that is finished, rarely updated and useful across a department or the whole company: oneaccord.sharepoint.com/sites/WelcomeOneAccord

It's the single source of truth for:

  • Official policies and procedures, including compliance documents and operational procedures.
  • Standards and reference guides, such as branding standards, report templates and technical specifications.
  • Sales and marketing resources: final, approved, public-facing documents.
  • Archival information: historical, non-client documents that are kept but no longer edited.

Your role on the Hub is to read, search and reference. You won't post or edit there. If you think something should be added or corrected, contact Jesse or Abby.

blocks.label: Find it now
blocks.instructions: Open the OneAccord Hub and take a few minutes to explore. Find where the company policies and the sales and marketing resources live.

blocks.html:
Hub vs. Teams channel files

PurposeWhereKey difference
Looking up final, approved informationSharePoint HubRead-only; managed by administrators
Actively editing or draftingTeams channel FilesYour team works on it together

Using the Hub strictly for official reference means everyone is reading the most current approved version.

The OneAccord Wins, Lessons, Resources team

This is our company-wide team for culture, knowledge sharing and questions that cross departments. The channels are open but lightly used, so your participation helps make them valuable.

ChannelUse it forHow to contribute
#WinsA light space to celebrateAdd reactions (🎉, ❤️) and short replies. For a win you want recognized at the all-team meeting, also post a Ninety.io Headline (Lesson 6).
#LessonsWhat you learned from a finished project: best practices, things to avoidNew post with a subject line. Invite discussion in replies.
#ResourcesNotes from events, articles and resources that could help the wider teamNew post with a clear subject. Use replies for discussion.
#EventsUpcoming events: training, gatherings, internal deadlinesPost events here. Check it regularly and react to confirm you saw it or will attend.

The etiquette from Lesson 3 matters even more in a company-wide space. Always reply in the thread, and use @Team only for messages that are truly relevant to every person in the company.

blocks.prompt: Where do you look for the approved, final version of a company policy?
options: A private chat with a colleague
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. The Hub is the home for official, approved documents.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: The Hub is the single source of truth for approved policies.

blocks.prompt: You spot an outdated document on the Hub. What do you do?
options: Contact Jesse or Abby so it can be updated
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. The Hub is read-only for staff, so changes go through Jesse or Abby.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: You can't edit the Hub. Contact Jesse or Abby.

blocks.prompt: Your team is actively revising a document together. Where should it live?
options: In the Teams channel's Files tab
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Active editing happens in the channel.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Documents being actively edited live in the Teams channel Files tab, not the Hub.

blocks.prompt: You want to share an article that could help the wider team. Where does it go?
options: A new post in #Resources with a clear subject line
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. #Resources is for sharing articles and knowledge.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Articles and resources go in #Resources with a clear subject line.

blocks.prompt: A project finished and you learned what to do differently next time. Where do you share it?
options: A private chat with your manager
An email to the whole firm
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. #Lessons is for knowledge transfer after a project.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: What you learned from a finished project goes in #Lessons.

blocks.prompt: An internal training session is coming up. Where do you post it?
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Upcoming events are posted in the #Events channel.
